title: Short Stuff: Currency Symbols
summary: Short Stuff episode with Josh and Chuck (Jerry sitting in for Dave) on the symbols of major world currencies. They cover the dollar sign and its origin from the Spanish peso (peso de ocho / pieces of eight, with the "P.S." abbreviation evolving into the double-stroke sign), the euro's curvy E with two horizontal lines based on the Greek epsilon, and its 2002 launch with common coin designs on one side. They discuss the British pound sterling as the oldest continuous currency, with the L for libra and the slash of unclear origin. They touch on the yen and yuan sharing a Y-with-lines symbol, with cash-only travel in Japan, and the Indian rupee's 2010 symbol designed by D. Udaya Kumar, combining Devanagari Ra, a Roman R, and the flag's parallel lines. Also mentioned: Canada's new $5 bill featuring Terry Fox. The hosts wrap by saying they have covered essentially every currency.

segments.title: Introduction to currency symbols
segments.summary: Josh introduces the short episode on currency symbols, noting Chuck picked the topic, with Jerry sitting in for Dave.

segments.title: The dollar sign
segments.summary: The dollar traces to the Spanish peso (peso de ocho, pieces of eight), which the US modeled its dollar on. The sign likely evolved from a 'P.S.' abbreviation for peso, with the S over the P and then the stroke versions. Josh jokes about an Ayn Rand theory of a U and S origin, which is presented as made up.

segments.title: The euro
segments.summary: The euro launched in 2002 after the EU formed in 1992. Its symbol is a curvy E with two horizontal lines, based on the Greek epsilon, and the two lines are said to represent stability. Original coins had a common side and national designs on the other.

segments.title: The pound sterling
segments.summary: The UK kept the pound instead of adopting the euro, though it was an EU founding member and left in 2020. The pound sterling is described as the oldest living continuous currency, traced to 928 CE under King Athelstan, with its origin tied to silver weight. The L stands for libra and the slash's meaning is unknown. Former British colonies use pounds with country designations.

segments.title: Yen, yuan, and cash in Japan and Canada
segments.summary: Discussion of a questionable claim about how the yen is pronounced in Japanese. The yen and Chinese yuan share a Y-style symbol with horizontal lines, and the yuan is a denomination of the renminbi. Josh advises that Japan is often cash only. Chuck mentions leftover Canadian cash, and the hosts note Canada's new $5 bill featuring Terry Fox.

segments.title: Indian rupee symbol
segments.summary: The rupee is an ancient currency. Its symbol was created through a 2010 design contest won by D. Udaya Kumar. Before that it was denoted by letters. The symbol combines Devanagari Ra, a Roman R, and parallel lines representing the Indian flag and an equals sign. Other countries using rupees are listed.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh says they have covered essentially every currency and the short stuff is over. Chuck gives the iHeartRadio production credit.
